migrationNotes: Spine: Send one cart into another and follow what is shared: momentum is split between the carts, signs let opposite momenta cancel, the energy account shows the crash has a cost, and the rule needs no outside push.

lesson.title: When carts stick together

steps.headline: What a crash does to momentum

lead.text: Start at the moment of the crash. When the front of one cart meets the back of the other, each pushes on the other. You met this in the lesson on pairs of forces: the two pushes are equal in size and opposite in direction, and they last exactly as long as the carts stay in contact.

Equal and opposite forces acting for the same time give equal and opposite impulses. One cart gains as much momentum as the other loses. If you add the two momenta together, the gain and the loss cancel, so the total is the same after the crash as before. This is called conservation of momentum.
For now we assume that the carts are pushed only by each other during the crash. The last screens come back to what happens when something else pushes too.

steps.headline: One total, shared by the stuck pair

lead.text: Now let the carts stick. After the crash they move as a single object with one velocity, and its mass is the two masses added together. Its momentum is that mass times the shared velocity, and by conservation this equals the total momentum before the crash.

Here u means a velocity before the crash and v is the shared velocity after it. Take a 1 kg cart moving at 5 m/s that locks onto a 4 kg cart standing still. The momentum before is 1 × 5 + 4 × 0 = 5 kg·m/s, because a cart at rest has none. Afterwards the 5 kg pair carries the same 5 kg·m/s, so its velocity is 5 ÷ 5 = 1 m/s.

afterFigure.text: The moving cart handed over some of its momentum, and the larger mass left it moving more slowly. The figure shows this crash, and a second one where the front cart is already rolling. Look at how the shared velocity changes with the starting velocity of the front cart.

lead.text: Both carts have the same mass, and the moving one is the only one with momentum.

reveal.text: The pair has twice the mass and the same momentum, so its speed is halved.

lead.text: Find the total momentum before the crash, then divide by the mass of the pair.

reveal.text: The momentum is 12 kg·m/s, shared by 6 kg, giving 2 m/s.

steps.headline: Carts that approach from opposite ends

lead.text: So far both carts moved the same way. Carts can also approach each other from opposite ends of the track, and then the signs matter. Take right as positive. A cart moving right has positive momentum and a cart moving left has negative momentum, so adding them lets one cancel part of the other.

Try a 2 kg cart moving right at 5 m/s and a 3 kg cart moving left at 2 m/s. Their momenta are 2 × 5 = +10 kg·m/s and 3 × (−2) = −6 kg·m/s. The total is +4 kg·m/s. The pair weighs 5 kg, so it moves at 4 ÷ 5 = 0.8 m/s to the right.

The sign of the total tells you which way the pair ends up, and a total of zero would leave it at rest. Always give each momentum its sign before you add, and divide by the combined mass only at the end.

steps.headline: A 3 kg cart at +4 m/s and a 1 kg cart at −8 m/s collide and stick. Find their shared velocity.

workedSteps.text: Add them and divide by the total mass.

steps.headline: A 2 kg cart at +6 m/s and a 4 kg cart at −3 m/s collide and stick. Find their shared velocity.

workedSteps.text: Add them and divide by the total mass.

steps.headline: What happens to the kinetic energy

lead.text: Momentum survives the crash and kinetic energy does not. Go back to the 1 kg cart at 5 m/s that locked onto the 4 kg cart. Before the crash its kinetic energy was ½ × 1 × 5² = 12.5 J. Afterwards the 5 kg pair moves at 1 m/s and has ½ × 5 × 1² = 2.5 J. The crash used up 10 J, four fifths of what there was.

The missing energy went into other forms. The couplings banged together and the metal deformed a little. The crash made a noise and warmed the carts. This is the energy account from the earlier lessons again: kinetic energy became thermal energy and sound. A collision that turns kinetic energy into other forms like this is called an inelastic collision, and carts that stick together lose the most they can.
The two rules do different jobs. Momentum gives you the speed of the pair, and the energy account tells you what the crash cost.
Work out the kinetic energy before the crash and after it, and compare.

reveal.text: The kinetic energy drops from 36 J to 12 J, so 24 J became other forms.

lead.text: The rule needs a condition. Total momentum stays the same only if no outside impulse acts on the two carts. The pushes the carts give each other are internal forces, and because they come in equal and opposite pairs they cancel in the total whatever their size. A push from outside brings an impulse that nothing cancels. A hand holding the first cart back would do it, and so would a rough floor dragging on the wheels.

On a smooth track a crash lasts so short a time that the impulse from friction is tiny beside the carts' momentum, and ignoring it is reasonable. The same reasoning applies to any crash between two objects, whether or not they stick. On any new problem, check first whether anything outside is pushing on the objects during the crash.
The carts push each other during the crash. The track and the air might push them as well.

reveal.text: Internal forces cancel in the total, so only a significant outside impulse could change it.

lesson.orientation: Conserve signed momentum across a sticking collision and account for the kinetic-energy change.
lesson.nextAction: Try the next idea, then return for a fresh problem after a delay.

blocks.text: On a smooth, level track a cart rolls towards a second cart that is standing still. The two are identical, and each has a coupling on its end. When they meet, the couplings lock and the pair rolls on as one.

The pair moves, but it moves more slowly than the first cart did. Something that belonged to the first cart has been shared with the second. In the last lesson you saw that a push lasting a certain time changes momentum, and in this crash each cart pushes on the other. That suggests a way to predict how fast the pair will go, before anyone has let go of the first cart.
We start with what a crash does to the momentum of two carts and use it to predict the speed of the pair. Afterwards we check the kinetic energy, which behaves differently.

intro.promise: By the end you'll find the speed of carts that stick, and say what happens to their kinetic energy.

recap.keyIdea: When carts stick, their total momentum is the same before and after, with each momentum given its sign. The pair's velocity is that total over the combined mass, and some kinetic energy turns into other forms.

blocks.text: You found that an 8 m/s cart hitting an identical cart at rest leaves the pair at 4 m/s. You also found that a 2 kg cart and a 4 kg cart with equal and opposite momenta stop each other completely.

recap.nextHook: That is the end of the course. Motion, forces, energy and momentum each answer a different question about the same carts and balls, and you can now bring all four to one problem.

questions.prompt: A 2 kg cart at +6 m/s hits a resting 4 kg cart and they stick. External impulse is negligible. Find their shared final velocity in m/s.
hints: Add both initial signed momenta.
The stuck carts have combined mass 6 kg.
Divide 12 by 6.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Total momentum is 2 × 6 + 4 × 0 = 12 kg·m/s; v = 12/(2 + 4) = 2 m/s.

questions.onCorrect: 2 m/s. Total momentum is conserved, so divide it by the combined mass.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the first cart's velocity. After sticking, the combined mass shares the momentum.
That divides by one cart's mass. Use the combined mass.

questions.prompt: A 2 kg cart at +6 m/s and a 4 kg cart at −3 m/s collide and stick. External impulse is negligible. Find their shared final velocity in m/s.
hints: Include the negative sign of the second velocity.
Add 12 and −12.
Divide the total momentum by 6 kg.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Initial momentum is 2 × 6 + 4 × (−3) = 0; final velocity is 0 m/s.

questions.onCorrect: 0 m/s. The two momenta are equal and opposite, so the total is zero and the pair stops.

misconceptions.feedback: That adds the two velocities and halves them. Add the momenta, then divide by the total mass.
The two momenta cancel exactly, so there is none left to give the pair a velocity.

questions.prompt: A 2 kg cart at 6 m/s hits a resting 4 kg cart. They stick and move at 2 m/s. How many joules of kinetic energy are converted into other forms?
hints: Calculate kinetic energy before and after contact.
Use the combined mass for the final state.
Subtract 12 J from 36 J.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Initial K = ½ × 2 × 6² = 36 J; final K = ½ × 6 × 2² = 12 J; decrease = 24 J.

questions.onCorrect: 24 J. Momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is not: 36 J before, 12 J after.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the kinetic energy afterwards. The question asks how much was converted.
That is the kinetic energy before. Subtract what is left afterwards.

questions.prompt: What condition justifies treating the total momentum of two colliding carts as unchanged by the crash?
hints: Separate internal collision forces from external influences.

acceptedIdeas: The external impulse on the two-cart system is negligible
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: The total momentum changes by external impulse, so negligible external impulse permits momentum conservation.

choices.label: The carts must have equal mass
The external impulse on the two-cart system is negligible
The carts must conserve kinetic energy

questions.onCorrect: When the external impulse on the system is negligible. Then only internal forces act, and they cancel in the total.

misconceptions.feedback: Equal masses are not needed. Any masses work if there is no external impulse.
Kinetic energy is not conserved in a sticking collision. The condition is about external impulse.

questions.prompt: A 3 kg cart at +4 m/s hits a resting 1 kg cart and they stick. External impulse is negligible. Find their shared final velocity in m/s.
hints: Find total initial momentum.
Use the combined mass after sticking.
Divide total initial momentum by the combined mass.
questions.onCorrect: 3 m/s. Total momentum over combined mass.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the moving cart's velocity. After sticking, the carts share the momentum.
That is the total momentum. Divide by the combined mass.

questions.prompt: In an isolated sticking collision, what is conserved across the collision?
hints: Apply the conservation rule to the whole system.

acceptedIdeas: Total momentum; kinetic energy may become other forms
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Internal forces exchange momentum between carts; total momentum remains fixed while some kinetic energy becomes other forms.

choices.label: Total momentum; kinetic energy may become other forms
Kinetic energy, but not total momentum

questions.onCorrect: Total momentum is conserved. Kinetic energy may become other forms such as heat and sound.

misconceptions.feedback: Each cart's momentum changes in a collision. The total is what stays fixed.
It is the reverse: total momentum is conserved, and kinetic energy is not.

questions.prompt: A cart moving at 8 m/s runs into an identical cart at rest and the two lock together. How fast does the pair move, in m/s?
hints: Compare how much mass is moving before and after the crash.
The total momentum is the same after the crash as before.
The same momentum is now carried by twice the mass.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Same momentum, twice the mass: 8 ÷ 2 = 4 m/s.

questions.onCorrect: 4 m/s. The moving cart's momentum is shared by twice the mass, so the speed halves.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the speed before. The carts now share the momentum, so each is slower.
That doubles the speed. The mass doubled, so the speed falls.

questions.prompt: A 2 kg cart moves at +9 m/s and hits a resting 1 kg cart. They stick together. What is their shared velocity, in m/s?
hints: Find the total momentum before.
The resting cart has no momentum.
Divide by the combined mass.
questions.onCorrect: 6 m/s. Total momentum before equals total momentum after, shared over the combined mass.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the moving cart's velocity. After sticking, the combined mass shares the momentum.
That is the total momentum. Divide by the combined mass.

questions.prompt: Why is the second cart's momentum negative?
hints: Read each choice against the situation before you answer.

acceptedIdeas: It moves in the negative direction.
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: It moves in the negative direction.

choices.label: It moves in the negative direction.
Momentum is always negative after a crash.

questions.onCorrect: Momentum takes the sign of the velocity. Leftward is negative when right is positive.

misconceptions.feedback: Mass is always positive. The sign comes from the direction of the velocity.
The sign depends on the direction of motion, not on a crash.

questions.prompt: A 1 kg cart at 4 m/s hits an identical resting cart and they stick, moving at 2 m/s. How many joules of kinetic energy are converted to other forms?
hints: Find the kinetic energy before.
Find it again for the pair afterwards.
Subtract the energy afterwards from the energy before.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Before: ½ × 1 × 16 = 8 J. After: ½ × 2 × 4 = 4 J. Lost: 4 J.

questions.onCorrect: 4 J. Half the kinetic energy became other forms, though momentum was conserved.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the kinetic energy before. Take away what is left afterwards.
Momentum is conserved, but kinetic energy is not in a sticking collision.

questions.prompt: A 4 kg cart at +5 m/s meets a 4 kg cart at −1 m/s. They stick. What is their shared velocity, in m/s?
hints: Give each momentum its own sign.
Add the two signed momenta.
Divide the total by the combined mass.
questions.onCorrect: +2 m/s. The negative momentum takes away from the positive one before you divide by the total mass.

misconceptions.feedback: That averages the velocities, ignoring the signs. Add the signed momenta instead.
That treats both momenta as positive. The second cart moves the other way.
